rv.q: Exuberant performances, gleeful silliness, and cleverly witty material make this adaptation a thoroughly entertaining evening.

The comic banter among the players and the players breaking the fourth wall to tickle audience members in the front row creates a constant eruption of laughter throughout the play as Scapin lies and cheats his way through the comedy to ironically resolve all of the relationships happily.

The play definitely has its moments, particularly those where the actors go off-script and involve the audience in some way. But there are definitely dead spots in this show, particularly a way-too-long chase scene at the end.

cn.t: Critics praise this inventive adaptation of Molière's farce for its energetic performances and clever updating. The production delivers high-spirited fun with actors clearly reveling in the comedic material.
